short: The fastest imperial expansion in history, from Spain to the Indus in ninety years.
full:
Mu'awiya, governor of Syria, took the caliphate in 661 at the end of the first Muslim civil war, moved the capital from Medina to Damascus and made the office hereditary in his family. Under his successors Arab armies completed the conquest of North Africa, crossed into Spain in 711, reached the Indus, and twice besieged Constantinople without taking it. Abd al-Malik gave the state an Arabic chancery, its own coinage in place of Byzantine and Persian issues, and the Dome of the Rock.

Governing a mostly non-Arab and still mostly non-Muslim population through a narrow Arab elite produced the grievance that destroyed the dynasty. The Abbasid revolution, built on discontent in Khurasan, defeated the last caliph Marwan II at the Great Zab in 750, and almost the whole family was hunted down and killed. One survivor, Abd al-Rahman, reached Spain and founded the emirate of Cordoba, which outlasted Damascus by nearly three centuries.
